note_out: Source opened only says Greek religion kept animistic elements; the spirits-to-gods sequence is an older evolutionary scheme, not stated outright.
No source found saying Aristotle's hylomorphic soul builds on animism; thematic parallel only.
Aristotle criticised the Forms and offered hylomorphic forms to salvage much of Plato's theory.
Marked Pythagorean influence on Plato is stated; page adds that the world of forms itself is Platonic, not Pythagorean.
Stoics: logos as active reason pervading and animating the universe.
Gospel of John identifies Christ as the incarnate Logos; John 1:1 quoted.
Old Testament is based primarily on the Hebrew Bible, with differences in order and contents.
Aquinas sought to synthesize Aristotelian philosophy with the principles of Christianity.
Listed under Scholasticism; Summa is a guide to Catholic theology.
SEP Dualism traces Christian adoption of Platonic soul-dualism before Descartes but does not state the derivation explicitly.
Motivated by dualist mind-body problem; associated with Descartes' Cartesian followers, notably Malebranche. Doctrine itself is older (al-Ghazali).
Leibniz opposed Cartesian substance dualism and found Descartes' interactionism unintelligible.
Extends Descartes' animal-automaton argument to humans and denies a separate soul; so it both builds on and opposes Descartes.
Innatism tied to Descartes; Locke is named the main antagonist of innate ideas.
Berkeley responded to Locke; his approach to empiricism was later called subjective idealism.
Kant credited Hume with awakening him from a dogmatic slumber, then countered Hume's empiricism.
Kant studied Leibniz and Wolff, then criticised Leibnizian-Wolffian rationalism; so partly against as well as builds.
Kant's 1784 essay: 'Sapere aude' as the motto of enlightenment.
Bentham's cited influences (Helvetius, Beccaria, Hume) are Enlightenment figures, but no opened page states the link in these words.
Hegel and others after Kant built upon and challenged Kant's work.
Hegel's absolute idealism; Spirit comes to fully comprehend its own freedom.
Proponents say it completes and extends Darwin; Mayr called the gene-as-object view non-Darwinian.
Darwin made the first suggestion of group selection in The Descent of Man.
Named after Darwin; selectionist theory of neuronal groups.
No source found tying Levin's work to cell theory; cell theory does not treat cells as cooperating agents.
Thematic parallel; pages opened name Leibniz and Huxley as precursors, not du Bois-Reymond. No influence shown.
SEP's epiphenomenalism entry discusses Chalmers 1996 and the hard problem.
Brentano's intentionality and descriptive psychology were inherited and developed by Husserl's phenomenology.
Freud is listed among Brentano's students at Vienna.
Pages opened name Wundt as founder of experimental psychology and James teaching it from 1875, but do not link them directly.
Behaviorism rejected introspection; page warns Wundt's own view is often misread, and Skinner's radical behaviorism treated introspection as behavior.
Kant influenced Husserl, who recast phenomenology as transcendental idealism.
Husserl, Heidegger and Merleau-Ponty named as inspiration for the embodiment thesis.
Russell found the paradox while examining Cantor's proof that there is no greatest cardinal.
Russell wrote to Frege in 1902 showing the paradox in Frege's system.
Wittgenstein read Frege, visited him in 1911; Frege sent him to Russell. The note's wording is a gloss.
Studied at Cambridge under Russell, 1911-1913.
Theorems apply to systems containing enough arithmetic, with Peano arithmetic the standard example.
Goedel's 1931 paper demonstrated the incompleteness of the system of Principia Mathematica.
Theorems are interpreted as showing Hilbert's program is impossible.
Intuitionism created partly in reaction to Cantor's set theory; Brouwer rejected actual infinity.
Brouwer's intuitionism opposed Hilbert's formalism.
SEP's Tarski and Tarski-truth entries do not mention Frege; any influence is indirect.
Frege's motivation resembled Leibniz's calculus ratiocinator; Frege denied having achieved that aim.
Turing worked on decidability starting from Goedel's incompleteness theorems.
Turing's 1936 paper negatively answered Hilbert's Entscheidungsproblem, shortly after Church.
Lambda-definable, general recursive and Turing-computable functions are equivalent.
Scheme has lambda calculus at its core and is the language used with SICP.
Von Neumann credited the fundamental conception to Turing; Eckert and Mauchly were unaware of Turing's work.
Turing turned to mathematical biology in 1951 and published the paper in 1952.
History pages present Turing's 1950 paper as a precursor to the 1956 founding, but do not state that the workshop drew on it.
Models computing non-Turing-computable functions; Turing's own 1938 oracle machines were the first.
Quantum computers add no computability power and can be simulated by a Turing machine.
Algorithmic information theory, founded by Solomonoff, is described as Shannon plus Turing; no page ties Solomonoff induction itself to Shannon.
Shannon was one of the four organizers and proposal authors.
